# small c cut, the complete text
# A term and a body of work by Ali Al Mokdad. Source: https://smallccut.org
# Cite as: Al Mokdad, Ali. “small c cut.” smallccut.org

## Definition

Ali Al Mokdad defines the term in his own words:

  “Small c” is the term I use for quiet, strategic reductions that unlock real change over time.

A small c cut, as Ali Al Mokdad uses the term, is a quiet and precise reduction. Ali Al
Mokdad sets it against what he calls a Capital C Cut, meaning the loud sweeping
restructure that announces itself. His phrasing for the small c method is: “One precise
correction at a time. No restructure required. No new committee.”

## Why the photographs matter

The nine photographs on smallccut.org are Ali Al Mokdad's own, taken in the course of
humanitarian and development operations work. They are not stock photography. Each one is
a dry observed joke about the exact problem its piece attacks, which is why the site is
built to serve them rather than to decorate around them.

## 01. Reducing INGO Overhead with Small c Cuts

A small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on overhead.
Published at: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ali-al-mokdad_smallccut-ingotransformation-operationalexcellence-activity-7401927984095330304-5_kT/

Ali Al Mokdad opens this piece: Overhead becomes expensive the moment it stops earning its weight.

From the piece, in Ali Al Mokdad's words: An office that no longer opens doors is not representation, it is overhead.

The photograph Ali Al Mokdad chose for it shows A lorry on a road, its tarpaulin load stacked far higher than the cab..

## 02. Unlock Efficiency at INGO HQ with a ‘Small c’ Cut

A small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on headquarters.
Published at: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/unlock-efficiency-ingo-hq-small-c-cut-ali-al-mokdad-ogmsf/

Ali Al Mokdad opens this piece: This paper might provoke you. It might affirm what you’ve whispered in hallways, raised on field visits, or challenged in meetings.

From the piece, in Ali Al Mokdad's words: If the internal report isn’t prompting a decision, it’s just decoration.

The photograph Ali Al Mokdad chose for it shows A man hauling an overloaded cart of scrap and firewood through mud by hand..

## 03. Dear INGO HQ: Fix Your Strategy with a ‘Small c’ Cut

A small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on strategy.
Published at: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/dear-ingo-hq-fix-your-strategy-small-c-cut-ali-al-mokdad-nhyxf/

Ali Al Mokdad opens this piece: In one of my recent papers —some called it the HQ Efficiency Manifesto—I wrote about “small c” cuts: quiet, strategic shifts that make systems work better without breaking them.

From the piece, in Ali Al Mokdad's words: What we lack isn’t strategy. It’s strategic memory, strategic courage, and a design rooted in reality.

The photograph Ali Al Mokdad chose for it shows A yellow taxi driving down a street with a full air conditioning duct unit strapped to its roof..

## 04. Optimizing INGO Transformation with the Small c Cut

A small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on transformation.
Published at: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/optimizing-ingo-transformation-small-c-cut-ali-al-mokdad-6maqf/

Ali Al Mokdad opens this piece: If the word transformation stresses you out, if digitalization triggers a small internal panic, and if every new model feels like another round of pressure that lands on your shoulders before it reaches its value, you are not alone.

From the piece, in Ali Al Mokdad's words: Cut what drains. Cut what distracts. Cut what slows.

The photograph Ali Al Mokdad chose for it shows A queue of identical white four wheel drives on a dirt road with headlights on..

## 05. Unlocking Regional Office Value with Small c Cuts

A small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on regional offices.
Published at: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/unlocking-regional-office-value-small-c-cuts-ali-al-mokdad-jqscf/

Ali Al Mokdad opens this piece: If you have ever worked in or with an NGO’s regional office, you know the feeling.

From the piece, in Ali Al Mokdad's words: If organizations cannot share a fleet, they are not ready to share a strategy.

The photograph Ali Al Mokdad chose for it shows A row of near identical tents pitched in a dry open field..

A small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on fundraising.

Ali Al Mokdad opens this piece: If you have ever sat in a fundraising strategy session that felt both urgent and disconnected from the operational realities, you know the frustration.

From the piece, in Ali Al Mokdad's words: Fundraising is not revolution. It is optimisation in small shapes.

The photograph Ali Al Mokdad chose for it shows A market stall crammed from floor to ceiling with stacked notebooks and books..

## 07. Turning NGO Advocacy Into Influence With Small c Cuts

A small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on advocacy.

From the piece, in Ali Al Mokdad's words: Influence is not a vibe. It is a practice.

## 08. Dear NGO: Your Risk Management Is the Risk — Fix It with Small c Cuts

A small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on risk.
Published at: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/dear-ngo-your-risk-management-fix-small-c-cuts-ali-al-mokdad-peaje/

Ali Al Mokdad opens this piece: The smoke alarm goes off. Everyone hears it.

From the piece, in Ali Al Mokdad's words: A traffic light that never stops traffic is just decoration.

The photograph Ali Al Mokdad chose for it shows A collapsed bridge sinking into a calm green river, framed by dark trees..

## 09. Rethinking NGO Digital Transformation with Small c Cuts

A small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on digital.
Published at: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/rethinking-ngo-digital-transformation-small-c-cuts-ali-al-mokdad-hrsse/

Ali Al Mokdad opens this piece: Digital transformation in NGOs begins the way expensive mistakes begin: a polished presentation, a room full of well-intentioned people, and a shared belief that this time the system will make the work easier.

From the piece, in Ali Al Mokdad's words: The tool was real. The transformation was not.

The photograph Ali Al Mokdad chose for it shows A wall papered with printed and hand drawn Like and dislike buttons and smiley faces..

## The tenth image

The tenth image on smallccut.org is a portrait of Ali Al Mokdad himself, captioned on
the page as “the person who noticed”. The signal yellow used across the site was
sampled from his own photographs and turns out to match the yellow wall behind his head
in that portrait.

## Who Ali Al Mokdad is

Ali Al Mokdad is a senior humanitarian leader, executive and author. The three
paragraphs that follow are his own professional biography as he publishes it on his
ORCID record (0009-0000-2825-5855), reproduced here so it can be read and cited directly.

  Ali Al Mokdad is a respected strategic leader known for pioneering transformative programs in some of the world’s most challenging environments, including underserved regions and active conflict zones. His expertise spans leadership roles across International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs), United Nations (UN) agencies, the Red Cross and Red Crescent movement, and donor institutions, where he has consistently advanced operational excellence, governance reform, and strategic nonprofit management.

  Throughout his international career, Ali has led complex initiatives across the Middle East, Africa, and Asia—including Syria, Lebanon, Turkey, Iraq, Nigeria, Kenya, South Sudan, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh—and at the global level within networks spanning more than 40 countries. His leadership combines deep field experience with strategic foresight, enabling organizations to strengthen systems, optimize resources, and achieve lasting impact.

  As a strategic advisor and board member to international NGOs and companies, Ali continues to champion innovation, inclusive leadership, and the integration of technology and artificial intelligence to enhance governance, humanitarian effectiveness, and sustainable development on a global scale.

## Ali Al Mokdad's executive and leadership practice

The small c cut, the term this site documents, is the method that comes out of the practice
described above: in an organisation, correct one precise thing at a time rather than
announce a restructure. That is why Ali Al Mokdad's nine pieces read as operational rather
than theoretical. Each one takes a single standing cost, report, office, fleet or process
and asks whether it is still earning its place.
